media.label: Electronic media (CD/DVD/USB) charge
media.value: different fees for different media 'as prescribed by law', each bounded by the actual cost of making the copy (direct, chargeable reproduction costs); a greater-than-established use of IT resources for the requested medium may support a special service charge
media.unit: USD per unit of media (ceiling: actual cost)
media.rule_type: Permission (media differential) / Prohibition (not above actual cost)
media.notes: Delegation followed: § 132-6.2(a) 'as prescribed by law' → no instrument exists for municipalities (search log in delegations_followed). Agency regime note: Governor's 2018 Cabinet guidance says no fee for records produced electronically (NC-9010) — not binding on cities.

delivery.label: Delivery: mail / handling / email / pickup
delivery.value: agencies 'may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies' (AG Guide); statute is silent on mailing/handling
delivery.unit: USD (soft standard: cost of mailing; guidance-level)
delivery.authority: N.C. Attorney General, Open Government Guide (2019) p. 20; N.C. Gen. Stat. § 132-6.2(b) (statute silent on postage)
delivery.notes: No handling fee, no email/pickup charge is authorized or addressed; email/pickup delivery has no reproduction cost beyond the copy itself.

certification.label: Certification / certified-copy charge
certification.rule_type: Permission (fees for certifying 'as provided by law')
certification.notes: Certified-copy fees are expressly carved out of the actual-cost ceiling ('Except as otherwise provided by law ... uncertified copy'). For municipalities the delegated 'law' could not be located; treat as city-set pending manual verification.

av.label: Audio/video: per recording, per minute, free minutes
av.value: for law-enforcement recordings (body-worn/dashboard etc.): a fee 'to offset the cost incurred by it to make a copy of a recording for release' that 'shall not exceed the actual cost of making the copy'; other audio/video: actual cost of making the copy (§ 132-6.2(b)); no per-minute rate and no free-minutes allowance
av.unit: USD per copy/recording (ceiling: actual cost of making the copy)
av.rule_type: Permission (LE agency may charge) / Prohibition (not above actual cost)
av.notes: Prior status 'delegated_to_regulation_or_schedule' not supported. § 132-1.4A(l) binds every 'law enforcement agency' incl. municipal police; § 132-1.4A recordings are not public records and follow the release/disclosure regime of that section (court order for release), but the copy fee is a plain…

commercial.label: Commercial-purpose schedule (surcharge %, labor becomes chargeable)
commercial.value: no commercial-purpose surcharge or schedule; a requester may not be required to disclose purpose or motive (§ 132-6(b)); GIS databases/data files: city furnishes copies 'at reasonable cost' and may condition an electronic copy on a written agreement that it will not be resold or used for trade or commercial purposes (§ 132-10)
commercial.unit: enum (commercial): none (surcharge 0 %; labor not made chargeable by purpose); GIS non-commercial-use agreement gate
commercial.rule_type: Prohibition (no purpose inquiry) / Permission (GIS written no-resale condition)
commercial.notes: Shape: no purpose-based pricing exists (a purpose statement cannot be required, NC-0002); the only commercial-purpose mechanism is record-specific — county/city GIS electronic copies at 'reasonable cost' (a soft standard distinct from § 132-6.2(b) 'actual cost') with an optional written no-commer…

waiver.label: Fee waiver: grounds, mandatory vs discretionary, purpose statement, written denial, appeal
waiver.rule_type: Permission (fees are 'may'; policy 'free or at minimal cost')
waiver.notes: No waiver grounds, no mandatory waiver, no purpose statement (purpose may not be required, NC-0002), no written-denial or waiver-appeal rule. Because charging is permissive and the policy is 'free or at minimal cost', a city may waive at its discretion (discretionary). The only fee-review path is…

waiver.forfeiture.label: Late response forfeits the fee
waiver.forfeiture.notes: No fee forfeiture for late response; N.C. has no fixed response deadline to be late against ('as promptly as possible', NC-0005). Searched: N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 132 (Public Records) in full at ncleg.gov (current through S.L. 2026-30), incl. §§ 132-1(b), 132-6, 132-6.1, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10…

repeat.label: Repeat / aggregated requests (carry-forward, aggregation threshold)
repeat.notes: No repeat-request carry-forward, aggregation threshold or anti-splitting rule in N.C. law or guidance. Searched: N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 132 (Public Records) in full at ncleg.gov (current through S.L. 2026-30), incl. §§ 132-1(b), 132-6, 132-6.1, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10; ch. 159 (§ 159-32.1); ncl…

fee.labor_charge.summary: When separation of confidential from nonconfidential information is necessary to permit access, the public agency bears the cost of separation.

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: An agency may not charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the agency of making the copy.
fee.actual_cost_basis.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of making the copy

fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: An agency may assess different fees for different media, as prescribed by law.

fee.certified_copy_charge.summary: A requester may request certified or uncertified copies; fees for certifying copies are as provided by law.

fee.special_service_charge.summary: Where a request requires extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, the agency may charge a reasonable special service charge (based on actual cost) in addition to duplication cost.
If an agency voluntarily elects, as a service, to create or compile a record, it may negotiate a reasonable charge for the service with the requester.
